# A genuine smooth singleton menu can still have convex-potential efficiency below Gamma

This upgrades the archived triangle-product individual-profile obstruction to the NEW positive-width, positive-buffer H objective. The source is genuinely deepest for every sufficiently small pair of positive parameters. All ambient orientations are certified, and the selected caps have exact smooth kernel base centroid equal to their single source. Nevertheless that prescribed actual menu has efficiency below \(\Gamma_2=4/9\) over the ENTIRE nonnegative normal-dependent convex physical-field cone.

This is not an OC counterexample and not a stationary bad-body example. Its purpose is to exclude an unjustified universal individual-source payment theorem after smoothing.

## 1. The actual lattice-complete body

Set \(n=d=2\), and
\[
v_0=(-1,-1),\quad v_1=(1,0),\quad v_2=(0,1),\qquad
B=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,v_1,v_2\}.
\]
Then
\[
B\cap\mathbb Z^2=\{0,v_0,v_1,v_2\}.
\]
For a direct check, write \(s=z_1+z_2\). Its defining inequalities are
\(-s\geq-1\), \(3z_1-s\geq-1\), \(3z_2-s\geq-1\).
They give \(-2\leq s\leq1\). At \(s=-2\) the only possibility is \(v_0\); at \(s=-1\) both coordinates would have to be nonnegative, impossible; at \(s=0\) both are nonnegative and hence zero; at \(s=1\) they give \(v_1,v_2\).

Let \(K\) be a triangle with area \(V>0\) and centroid \(g\), and take \(C=B\times K\). Its four actual fibers are all \(K\), and total mixed volume is \(4V\). The tied profile \(f_H\) is independent of the base. The covariance norm and this profile are invariant under every affine barycentric permutation of \(K\).

Use the uniform outward kernel \(\Psi(t)=\min(1,\max(0,1+t))\), buffer \(\epsilon>0\), and width \(h>0\). Denote the own-fiber smooth depth at \(x\) by
\[
\theta_{\epsilon,h}(x)=
\inf_{u\ne0}\int_K
\Psi\!\left(\frac{u\cdot(X-x)+\epsilon f_H(x)\Gamma(u)}
 {h\Gamma(u)}\right)\,dX.
\]
Write \(q_{\epsilon,h}=\theta_{\epsilon,h}(g)\).

The own smooth superlevel sets are convex, and barycentric permutations preserve them. Averaging the permutation orbit of any \(x\) gives \(g\); hence \(g\) maximizes \(\theta_{\epsilon,h}\). For sufficiently small positive parameters all maximizers remain in a uniform own core, by the uniform slab comparison with ordinary depth. Strict own concavity of \(f_H\), an attained proper minimizing direction and positive smooth threshold derivative then make that maximizer unique, exactly as in the own-fiber part of the smooth parity proof. Moreover
\[
q_{\epsilon,h}\longrightarrow (4/9)V,
\qquad q_{\epsilon,h}<V
\]
for all sufficiently small parameters.

## 2. Exact certification against every ambient cap

At the middle source \(Y=(0,g)\), let \(N=(a,u)\), \(u\ne0\), be any through-source smooth cap. Let \(X\) be uniform in \(K\), and let \(X_0,X_1,X_2\) be its three cyclic barycentric permutations. Then \(\sum_jX_j=3g\), every \(X_j\) is uniform, and \(\sum_jv_j=0\). The three outer-fiber margins have sum
\[
\sum_j[a\cdot v_j+u\cdot(X_j-g)+\epsilon f_H(g)\Gamma(u)]
=3\epsilon f_H(g)\Gamma(u)>0.
\]
At least one margin is nonnegative for every sample, so its kernel value is exactly one. Therefore the total outer-fiber smooth capture is at least \(V\). The own contribution is at least \(q_{\epsilon,h}\).

Conversely, choose any own minimizing direction at \(g\). A sufficiently large finite base tilt exposing a chosen outer vertex captures its whole fiber, misses the other two outer fibers with saturation margin, and leaves the middle contribution unchanged. Hence the middle mixed smooth depth is exactly
\[
Q_{\epsilon,h}=V+q_{\epsilon,h}. \tag{1}
\]
Pure-base closed caps through base zero capture the whole middle fiber and at least one outer fiber; their mass is at least \(2V>Q_{\epsilon,h}\), so they do not affect (1).

At an outer base, exposure isolates its own smooth contribution, so its maximum depth is \(q_{\epsilon,h}\). At any middle point \(x\), the same large-tilt construction gives depth at most \(V+\theta_{\epsilon,h}(x)\). Consequently \(Y=(0,g)\) is the UNIQUE actual global deepest point. This proves global criticality, rather than merely checking a stationary menu.

## 3. A finite actual menu with constant outer profile

Choose an own minimizing direction \(u_0\), normalized by \(\Gamma(u_0)=1\), and its cyclic barycentric orbit \(u_0,u_1,u_2\). The orbit consists of minimizing directions, has zero sum, and has equal smooth threshold coareas \(S>0\). Also \(\nabla_x f_H(g)=0\).

Let the linear base forms be
\[
\ell_0(z)=-z_1-z_2,\quad
\ell_1(z)=3z_1-z_1-z_2,\quad
\ell_2(z)=3z_2-z_1-z_2.
\]
They take value \(2\) at the matching \(v_j\), and \(-1\) at the other vertices. Give cap \(j\) the base normal \(T\ell_j\), with finite \(T\) large enough that the matching outer fiber is saturated at one and the other outer fibers at zero. One common \(T\) works for all three directions and all sufficiently small parameters, by compactness after \(\Gamma\)-normalization.

All three caps have mass (1). Their continuous balance weights are \(\rho_j=1/3\), and their response weights are also \(1/3\) because all their coareas are equal. Their smooth kernel is supported only on the middle fiber, so the exact base centroid is zero for each cap. Their profile \(W_{\epsilon,h}\) equals \(1/3\) on every outer normal bundle. Its middle restriction is the cyclic own smooth profile \(W^0_{\epsilon,h}\).

## 4. Uniform control over the entire convex field cone

The ordinary triangle centroid has exactly three minimizing oriented directions, the canonical vertex caps. Here is an elementary equality check. A one-vertex through-centroid cap has edge intercept ratios \(\alpha,\beta\leq1\) satisfying \(1/\alpha+1/\beta=3\). Its area fraction \(\alpha\beta\) is at least \(4/9\), with equality only at \(\alpha=\beta=2/3\). The opposite two-vertex cap has area at least \(1/2\). Thus equality occurs exactly in the three canonical directions.

Uniform slab comparison on the compact circle \(\Gamma(u)=1\) implies that every own smooth minimizing direction approaches this three-element set as \((\epsilon,h)\to(0,0)\). Relabeling its cyclic orbit, the middle boundary profile therefore differs from the canonical triangle profile \(W^0\) only in sets \(E_{\epsilon,h}\) whose intersections with each edge have normalized total length \(\eta_{\epsilon,h}\to0\). These sets lie near edge parameters \(1/3\) and \(2/3\), and hence in \([1/4,3/4]\) for small parameters. This follows directly from uniform convergence of the three affine margins, since the limiting margins have nonzero edge slopes at their zeros.

For any nonnegative convex function \(F\) on \([0,1]\) and \(t\in[1/4,3/4]\), Jensen on \([t-1/4,t+1/4]\) gives
\[
F(t)\leq2\int_0^1F(s)\,ds.
\]
Thus
\[
\int_{E_{\epsilon,h}}F\leq2\eta_{\epsilon,h}\int_0^1F.
\tag{2}
\]
This estimate is uniform over arbitrarily steep convex functions; mere unweighted convergence of profiles would not suffice.

On each triangle edge, the canonical profile is
\(1/3+(1/3)1_{[1/3,2/3]}\). Convexity gives
\[
\int_0^1F\,W^0\leq(4/9)\int_0^1F:
\]
indeed \(2F(t+1/3)\leq F(t)+F(t+2/3)\) for \(0\leq t\leq1/3\), and integration bounds the middle-third integral by one third of the total. Combining this with (2) proves
\[
\int_{\partial K}\Phi(n,0,x)W^0_{\epsilon,h}\,dS
\leq(4/9+2\eta_{\epsilon,h})I_0,
\tag{3}
\]
where \(I_0=\int_{\partial K}\Phi(n,0,x)\,dS\), for EVERY nonnegative normal-dependent physical field convex in \((z,x)\).

Let \(I_j=\int_{\partial K}\Phi(n,v_j,x)\,dS\) and \(R=\sum_jI_j\). Since all four fibers and their normal bundles are identical, Jensen at the same physical \(x,n\) gives \(I_0\leq R/3\). The entire field efficiency is consequently at most
\[
\frac{(4/9+2\eta_{\epsilon,h})I_0+R/3}{I_0+R}
\leq\frac{1+4/9+2\eta_{\epsilon,h}}4
=\frac{13}{36}+\frac{\eta_{\epsilon,h}}2. \tag{4}
\]
For sufficiently small positive parameters, \(\eta_{\epsilon,h}<1/6\), so (4) is STRICTLY below \(4/9\). A constant field tends to equality at \(13/36\), showing that the limiting optimum is exactly that value.

## 5. Scope

This is an actual positive-width body with a unique deepest base, exact smooth kernel centroids, proper active caps, a finite balanced critical menu, and a rigorous upper bound on the full convex-potential cone. Therefore the numerical payment cannot follow merely from those facts.

The normalized depth tends to \(13/36\), well above the OC target \( (4/9)/4=1/9\). The body is not asserted to minimize the positive-parameter body objective, and its finite-base volume quotas are not those of a strict minimal bad family. Other actual critical menus may pay. A valid general route must retain the low-depth/minimal-body information or exploit favorable menu selection, rather than assert a universal individual \(\Gamma_d\) transfer for every smooth singleton menu.
